claims.explanation: Skipping is appropriate. C01 is a structural asymptotic assertion: each module has constant-size matrices under fixed d_enc, d_model, and action size, so total parameters grow O(n). E04 and Figure B.1 discuss this argument, while their parameter entries are symbolic multiples of m and qualitative growth descriptions rather than numeric counts. Numeric finite-task comparisons cannot establish constant module size or universal linear asymptotic growth; a monotonic or endpoint property would be a different claim.

The six metric-specific best-baseline properties preserve both P(T) and FTr for Meta-World, SpaceInvaders, and Freeway, using ge to allow the stated equality. Table 1 supplies all five baseline methods plus CompoNet under the ten-seed, 1M-step-per-task SAC/PPO sequence conditions. Excluding RT is correct because it is a reference-transfer statistic, not one of the five compared methods. No sequence or performance/transfer metric is omitted; the SpaceInvaders performance tie with FT-N at 0.99 remains allowed rather than incorrectly converted to strict superiority.

Skipping is appropriate for the complete three-scenario claim. E03 and Figure 4 provide scenario (i) informative-policy attention and scenario (iii) uninformative-policy/internal-policy behavior, with approximate returns, attention patterns, and matching rates. They do not provide a complete numeric relation establishing scenario (ii)'s general ability to learn a useful function of previous policies. Reducing the claim to the two available final returns or dominant-attention observations would omit one named scenario and the asserted mechanisms.

Skipping is appropriate. C04 combines O(n²) theoretical complexity, slower empirical inference growth through 300 tasks, and an architectural explanation involving parallel attention rather than sequential lateral connections. Figure 3 separates main-figure approximate timings at d_enc=64 and action size 6 from appendix timings at d_enc=39 and action size 4 through 300 tasks. Lower times at selected points are not a growth-rate or complexity proof, and merging those configurations would violate scope. The reported relation catalog cannot express the whole growth-and-mechanism assertion.

The corrected skip appropriately preserves the whole original claim rather than declaring only its directional prerequisite. Table 1 supplies FTr>RT in Meta-World, SpaceInvaders, and Freeway (0.01>−0.06, 0.74>0.70, and 0.80>0.67), and Figure D.2 explains the single-previous-task fine-tuning reference. However, E01/E02's aggregate transfer measurements and E03's informative/non-informative predecessor scenarios do not establish simultaneous compositional use of multiple previous tasks. The statement retains that mechanistic assertion, while its FTr≤RT falsifier supplies a refutation condition rather than an equivalence proving the mechanism from a positive comparison. The revised specification removes the partial C05 declaration, and the revised outcome explicitly documents why no installed reported relation expresses the full conjunctive claim.
